paper.title: The Sample Complexity of Uniform Approximation for Multi-Dimensional CDFs and Fixed-Price Mechanisms

settings.name_in_paper: Learning a uniform approximation of an n-dimensional CDF over a uniform grid G_K with one-bit feedback
unmapped: Goal: output a function uniformly epsilon-approximating the CDF P(X<=x) at all points of a uniform grid G_K of resolution 1/K over [0,1]^n
Feedback is the single bit I[X_t <= x_t] for i.i.d. X_t ~ D on [0,1]^n and query x_t
Arbitrary distribution D on [0,1]^n (no density assumption)
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t$, an independent sample $X_t \sim \cD$ is drawn, we select a query point $x_t \in [0,1]^n$, and we observe the single bit $\mathbb{I}[X_t \le x_t]$, where the inequality is component-wise. Our goal is to use a minimal number of rounds (queries/samples) in order to learn a function $\tilde{P}: [0,1]^n \to [0,1]$ that, with high probability, uniformly approximates the true CDF

settings.name_in_paper: Uniform approximation of an n-dimensional CDF over [0,1]^n for distributions with bounded density
unmapped: Goal: uniform epsilon-approximation of the CDF over all of [0,1]^n
Distribution D admits a density bounded by sigma_dens (known to the algorithm, used to set the grid)
settings.definition_quote: We assume that the probability distribution $\cD$ has \emph{bounded density}, which means that it admits a  probability density function $d: [0,1]^n \to \mathbb{R}$ that is upper bounded by some constant $\sigma > 0$ everywhere.

settings.name_in_paper: Sample complexity of learning fixed-price mechanisms in small markets
unmapped: Small market with n_s sellers and n_b buyers (n agents); valuations V ~ joint distribution on [0,1]^n; learner posts price vector p in [0,1]^n
Feedback is only the binary trade outcome Trade(V_t,p_t)
Objective E[Trade(V,p)] f(p) with known L-Lipschitz (l1) utility f: [0,1]^n -> [0,1] (e.g. revenue)
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t$, a valuation vector $V_t \in [0,1]^n$ is independently drawn from the probability distribution $\mathcal{V}$, we choose a mechanism ${p}_t \in [0,1]^n$, and we observe $\Trade({V}_t, {p}_t)$ as feedback.

settings.name_in_paper: Regret minimization for fixed-price mechanisms in small markets
unmapped: Small market fixed-price mechanisms with n agents; feedback is the binary trade outcome only
Reward E[Trade(V,p)] f(p) with known L-Lipschitz f: [0,1]^n -> [0,1]
settings.definition_quote: we are given a time horizon $T \in \mathbb{N}$ and the goal is to minimize the regret defined as: \mathsf{REG}_T \coloneq T \cdot \max_{p \in [0,1]^n} \mathbb{E}_{V \sim \mathcal{V}}[\Trade(V,p)] f(p) - \sum_{t \in [T]} \mathbb{E}_{V \sim \mathcal{V}}[\Trade(V,p_t)] f(p_t).

algorithms.name: RHI + CGE (Representative Hyperrectangles Identification with MCE/BinS, then Compute Grid Estimate)
Bounded-density extension of RHI+CGE (grid K = 2 sigma n / epsilon)
Grid CDF estimation + argmax over grid of P_tilde(p) f(p)

symbols.K_grid: inverse grid resolution: grid G_K has K^n points with spacing 1/K
symbols.c_n: unspecified absolute constant in the O(n) exponent

conditions: approximation required only at points of the uniform grid G_K
log2 K assumed integer for exposition
tuning: RHI run with internal accuracy epsilon' = epsilon / (2^{n+3} sqrt(n ln(4K/delta)) (log2 K)^n)

source.label: theo: main
source.quote: There exists an algorithm that, given an accuracy $\epsilon > 0$, a confidence $\delta \in (0,1)$, and a uniform grid $\mathcal{G}_K$ over $[0,1]^n$ of resolution $1 / K$ (with $K \in \mathbb{N}$), uses $\frac{1}{\epsilon^3}\log(K/\delta)^{\mathcal{O}(n)}$ queries and outputs a function $\widetilde P: \mathcal{G}_K \to [0,1]$ such that, with probability at least $1-\delta$, the following holds: |P(X<=x) - P~(x)| <= epsilon for all x in G_K.

results.notes: Paper's n is the dimension (d). The O(n) in the exponent is encoded via unspecified constant c_n. Proof gives explicit count 2^{n-1}(4 log2 K)^{n+2} M^3 / eps^3. Corollary 6.1 restates the same bound for trade probabilities in small markets via an affine transformation (not recorded separately). Compute: the paper says CGE is a polynomial-time estimator.

symbols.sigma_dens: upper bound on the probability density of D
symbols.c_n: unspecified absolute constant in the O(n) exponent

conditions: D admits a density bounded by sigma_dens
tuning: apply Theorem 3.1 with epsilon/2 and K = 2 sigma n / epsilon

source.label: theo: mainSmooth
source.quote: Assume that the distribution $\cD$ admits density bounded by $\sigma > 0$. Then, there exists an algorithm that, given an accuracy $\epsilon > 0$ and a confidence $\delta \in (0,1)$, uses $\frac{1}{\epsilon^3}\log(\sigma n/(\epsilon\delta))^{\mathcal{O}(n)}$ samples and outputs a function $\widetilde P : [0,1]^n \to [0,1]$ such that, with probability at least $1-\delta$: ... for all x in [0,1]^n.

results.notes: sigma here is a density bound, not a sub-Gaussian parameter; renamed sigma_dens.

symbols.c_n: unspecified absolute constant in the O(n) exponent

conditions: f: [0,1]^n -> [0,1] is known and L-Lipschitz w.r.t. l1 norm (one-sided Lipschitz suffices)

source.label: thm:pricing
source.quote: There exists an algorithm that, given an accuracy $\epsilon>0$, a confidence $\delta \in (0,1)$, and a $L$-Lipschitz function $f: [0,1]^n \to [0,1]$, uses $\log(nL/(\delta\epsilon))^{\mathcal{O}(n)}\frac{1}{\epsilon^3}$ queries and outputs a solution $p^\star \in [0,1]^n$ such that, with probability at least $1-\delta$, ... >= max_p E[Trade(V,p)] f(p) - epsilon.

results.notes: Paper claims this is tight for constant n, matching Kleinberg-Leighton one-dimensional lower bound.

symbols.c_n: unspecified absolute constant in the O(n) exponent

source.label: theo: mainFixedPriceRegret
source.quote: There exists an algorithm that, given a number of rounds $T \in \mathbb{N}$ and a $L$-Lipschitz function $f: [0,1]^n \to [0,1]$, achieves regret: REG_T := T max_p E[Trade(V,p)] f(p) - sum_t E[Trade(V,p_t)] f(p_t) <= \log(nLT)^{\mathcal{O}(n)} T^{3/4}.

results.notes: Regret defined via expected utilities (pseudo-regret). Proof shows the bound w.p. 1-1/T and says the statement follows; the probability type in the statement itself is not explicit.
